title: Dietitian Salary Guide: Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage
description: Learn how to calculate a dietitian salary from hourly award rates, including casual loading, super, and tax. Compare the Health Professionals Award with the National Minimum Wage.

faqs.q: What is the typical dietitian salary under the Health Professionals Award?
faqs.a: A dietitian is usually classified as a Health Professional under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020. The minimum hourly rate for Level 2 (common entry point) is $28.03 per hour as of 1 July 2026. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, that equates to $1,065.20 per week and an annual gross of approximately $55,390.40. More experienced dietitians at higher levels earn more, up to Level 9 at $39.42 per hour.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a dietitian's pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 2 dietitian, that adds $7.01 per hour, making the casual rate $35.04 per hour. This loading is paid instead of entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. When calculating annual pay, use the casual rate × hours per week × 52, but remember that casual hours may vary.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a dietitian?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings at the super guarantee rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a full-time dietitian earning $55,390.40 per year, the employer would contribute an additional $6,646.85 into super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from the employee's pay; it is an extra cost for the employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding a Dietitian Salary from Hourly Award Rates

If you're a dietitian or considering the profession, knowing how to convert an hourly award rate into a weekly, fortnightly, or annual salary is essential. This guide uses the latest Fair Work Ombudsman rates under the **Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020** to show you exactly what a **dietitian salary** looks like, and how it compares to the National Minimum Wage.

### The Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The standard calculation for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a full-time employee works 38 ordinary hours per week, as defined in the award. For part-time or casual roles, the same formula applies but with fewer or variable hours. Always use the base hourly rate (before casual loading) for full-time and part-time employees.

### Dietitian Salary Under the Award

Dietitians are classified as Health Professionals under the award. The minimum rates from 1 July 2026 are set out in the award. A common entry level for a graduate dietitian is **Level 2**, with a minimum hourly rate of **$28.03**. Here's how that translates:

- **Weekly**: $28.03 × 38 hours = **$1,065.20**
- **Fortnightly**: $1,065.20 × 2 = **$2,130.40**
- **Annual gross**: $1,065.20 × 52 = **$55,390.40**

More experienced dietitians at Level 8 or Level 9 earn significantly more—up to $39.42 per hour (Level 9, pay point 3), giving an annual salary of about $77,900.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rate

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. The award rate for a Level 2 dietitian is **$1.59 per hour higher**, reflecting the specialised skills required. Employers must pay at least the award rate, not the lower National Minimum Wage, for award-covered employees.

### Casual Loading and Its Effect

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 2 dietitian:

- Casual rate: $28.03 × 1.25 = **$35.04 per hour**
- Weekly (if working 38 hours): $35.04 × 38 = **$1,331.52**
- Annual: $1,331.52 × 52 = **$69,239.04**

Note that casual loading is paid instead of paid leave entitlements. When using [the timesheet](/), you can check the box to add 25% casual loading on top of the base rate—never type a rate that already includes loading.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is currently **12%** of ordinary earnings, paid by the employer on top of your salary. For a full-time dietitian earning $55,390.40:

- Super contribution: $55,390.40 × 12% = **$6,646.85**
- Total cost to employer: $62,037.25

The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830** per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional benefit.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Tax-free threshold: $0 – $18,200
- 15%: $18,201 – $45,000
- 30%: $45,001 – $135,000
- 37%: $135,001 – $190,000
- 45%: above $190,000

Plus Medicare levy of 2% (single reduction thresholds from 2025–26 apply). For a $55,390.40 annual gross, estimated tax is about $7,468 and Medicare $1,108, leaving a take-home of around **$46,814** per year. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a detailed breakdown.

### Fortnightly Pay Periods

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a full-time dietitian at Level 2:

- Fortnightly gross: $1,065.20 × 2 = **$2,130.40**
- Fortnightly after tax (approx): $1,800.50

This helps with budgeting and aligns with the award's provision for weekly or fortnightly pay.

### Key Points to Remember

- Always use the award rate for your classification, not the National Minimum Wage, if you're covered by the Health Professionals Award.
- The formula **hourly × 38 × 52** gives annual gross, but actual hours may vary for part-time or casual roles.
- Super is paid on top at 12%.
- Casual loading is 25% extra but replaces leave entitlements.
- For personalised calculations, refer to [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

This guide is an estimate. Your actual pay may differ due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or enterprise agreements. Always check your award or consult the Fair Work Ombudsman.
